clue.text: Volatile African oil state

indicators.note: something volatile is unstable and liable to change, so the letters of the next two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A commentator describes an unstable oil-producing nation in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volatile' sounds like a political or market description, but it signals rearranging AFRICAN OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: California is one of the fifty constituent states of the USA.

clue.text: English university with data on east Oregon city

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or data
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An English university with research data on an Oregon city.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British English for information, as in 'get the gen on something'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene is a city in the US state of Oregon, home of the University of Oregon.

clue.text: Killer of two donkeys at home

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, so two of them give the word twice over
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Someone who killed a pair of donkeys while staying in.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, typically one who kills a prominent person.

clue.text: Lake covered by grotesque scaly monster

indicators.note: a thing covered by another sits within it, so the lake's letter goes inside the rearranged word
grotesque means distorted, so the letters of scaly are twisted into a new order

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A hideous scaly creature lurks beneath the waters of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grotesque' turns SCALY into SCYLA, and 'covered by' places L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scylla is the many-headed sea creature of Greek myth facing Charybdis across a strait.

clue.text: Not working (tired out), relaxed

parts.note: a machine or system that is down has stopped functioning
beat is informal for exhausted

explanation.surface: Someone off work and exhausted, now feeling at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Downbeat can mean casual or low-key in manner, besides its gloomier sense.

clue.text: Fruit couple picked up

indicators.note: picked up as by the ear, so the word is chosen for how it is heard

parts.note: a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: Two pieces of fruit collected from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a familiar orchard fruit, sweet and tapering towards the stalk.

clue.text: Speaks about universal children's game

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for speaks goes round the letter

parts.note: to state is to speak or declare
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Someone talks about a game every child knows.
explanation.walkthrough: STATUES is a party game, often played as musical statues, where children freeze when the music stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Statues is a party game in which players must freeze motionless when the music halts.

clue.text: Succeed in changing e.g. hems? I can, using this!

definitions.text: Succeed in changing e.g. hems? I can, using this!

indicators.note: in places the word for succeed inside the rearranged letters
changing shows the letters that follow are being altered into a new order

parts.note: the abbreviation e.g. contributes its two letters
to win is to succeed

explanation.surface: A tailor boasts that altering hems is easy with the right equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' produces SEGMACHINE, and 'in' takes the word for succeed inside it; read whole, the clue also describes what the device is for.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewing machine is the device used for stitching and altering garments such as hems.

clue.text: Detailed photograph of bar at university

parts.note: to bar a door is to close it
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A detailed snapshot taken in a bar on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a shot taken near the subject, showing it in fine detail.

clue.text: Secretive person after plain food as a hangover cure?

indicators.note: after places the secretive person behind the plain

parts.note: a prairie is a broad grassy plain
an oyster is someone who keeps their mouth shut, like the closed shellfish

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped person eats simple fare to recover from a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like an adjective describing the food, but it is a noun meaning open grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie oyster is a raw egg swallowed whole with seasoning, a traditional remedy after heavy drinking.

clue.text: The British government, with Heath ill, reshuffled

indicators.note: a government reshuffle moves people around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cabinet reshuffle in the days of a sick Prime Minister Edward Heath.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath is Edward Heath, UK Prime Minister 1970-74; 'reshuffled', the cabinet term, is borrowed as the signal and makes HITEHALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitehall is the London street of ministries, used by metonymy for the civil service and government.

clue.text: Opera in general student shunned

indicators.note: shunned means avoided, so the student's letter is left out

parts.note: general means normal or usual
L stands for learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student avoids going to a well-known opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is Bellini's tragic opera about a druid priestess.

clue.text: What may be round head of steer caught by one rustling?

definitions.text: What may be round head of steer caught by one rustling?

indicators.note: caught by means held within, so the round letter and the steer's initial go inside the shuffled word
rustling suggests stirring things up, so the letters of one are mixed

parts.note: O is a round shape

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A cattle thief lassoes a steer around its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rustling' rearranges the word into NOE, and 'caught by' sets the round letter and the steer's initial inside it; read whole, the clue pictures the lasso itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a running loop of rope, like a lasso thrown over an animal's head.

clue.text: Put on glasses approaching end of corridor leading to actors' entrance

parts.note: to put on a play is to stage it
OO looks like a pair of spectacles

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone dons spectacles walking down a corridor toward the actors' door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on glasses' reads as donning spectacles; OO is the visual shorthand for a pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage door is the backstage entrance to a theatre used by performers and staff.

clue.text: Rook completed attack

parts.note: over means finished or completed
a charge is an attack

explanation.surface: A chess rook completes an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like the chess piece, but it is the verb meaning to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to cheat them, especially by asking too high a price.

clue.text: Large house over in Reno is Namibian's

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the concealed letters read backwards
in shows the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A grand residence in Reno belongs to someone from Namibia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' conceals NOISNAM in 'reNO IS NAMibian's' and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansion is a large, imposing residence.

clue.text: Head knocked off toy soldier in battle

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, knocked off so it is removed

parts.note: to toy with something is to tinker with it
a man is a soldier of the ranks

explanation.surface: A toy soldier loses its head during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toy' is a verb here (to tinker), not the noun the surface suggests; 'Head knocked off' removes the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkerman was an 1854 Crimean War battle fought by British and French forces against Russia.

clue.text: Angry about article? That will teach you!

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the angry word goes round the article

parts.note: sore is informal for angry or annoyed
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone is cross about a newspaper piece and feels vindicated.
explanation.definitionFit: 'So there' is a retort of triumphant defiance, telling someone they have been put in their place.

clue.text: Wisdom shown by commander in South London, say

indicators.note: in places the commander's title within the South and London pieces

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
London is an example of a city
an aga is a Turkish military commander

explanation.surface: A wise commander posted in South London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South London' looks like one place; S and CITY are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity is sound judgement and keen insight, a close synonym of wisdom.

clue.text: 50 tucked into marvellous meat product

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so the numeral goes within the word for marvellous

parts.note: cracking is British informal for excellent
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Half a hundred servings eaten of a wonderful pork dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating, but it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackling is the crisp roasted skin of pork, a much-loved part of a Sunday roast.

clue.text: Released children, first of detainees

parts.note: issue means offspring, as in 'died without issue'

indicators.note: first of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Children are set free, the first among the detainees.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something is to put it out or release it publicly.

clue.text: Staggering film …

definitions.meaning: unsteady on one's feet, as a boxer after a blow
The 1976 boxing film starring Sylvester Stallone

explanation.surface: A stunning film, with the ellipsis running on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky describes someone tottering and also titles the famous boxing picture.

clue.text: Go to service

definitions.meaning: to ... to a place is to go there

explanation.surface: An instruction to attend a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Repair has two senses: to fix something, and to betake oneself somewhere.

clue.text: … of victor losing face in ring

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front letter, which is lost

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: Continuing the ellipsis: a film about a champion humiliated in the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing face' looks like humiliation, but it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner is the ring of a target just outside the bull, in archery and shooting.

clue.text: Ordered in one, a tavern

indicators.note: in shows the answer is concealed in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something was ordered at one particular pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a verb about buying drinks, but it means tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means tidy and in good order.

clue.text: Bootlicker, extremely smarmy chap, not unexpectedly

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of the following word
unexpectedly suggests things turning out other than planned, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smarmy man who, surprisingly, isn't a toady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives SY from smarmy; 'unexpectedly' rearranges CHAP NOT into COPHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant is a fawning flatterer, colloquially a bootlicker.

clue.text: Greek character, celebrity, backed issue

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so these pieces read in reverse

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A Greek celebrity funds a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like financial support but reverses ETA NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source.

clue.text: Set off first of rockets held by one of Pooh's friends

indicators.note: held by means contained within, so the letter goes inside the friend's name

parts.note: Tigger is the bouncy tiger in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh stories

indicators.note: first of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A rocket launch begun by one of Winnie-the-Pooh's companions.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off or cause it to start.
